Call only graph_capabilities, graph_audit, graph_run, and graph_query yourself; do not call bash or read. Audit the plan with graph_audit until it is admitted, run it with graph_run, then reply with only the stop reason, the heading, and how many times the loop edge fired.

The capabilities list shows no categories, and tools: grep, read. Hmm, categories is empty — nodes have kinds execution/verification etc. The categories listed are for "category" field maybe. Let me just build the plan with tools restricted to read.

Note depth: current 0, max 1 — delegation depth. Nodes run as subagents at depth 1, fine.

Let me build the plan.

Plan format dsh-graph/v1:
- id: "guide-heading"
- level: "L2"
- goal: report first heading of GUIDE.md
- runInputs: [] — probably empty array acceptable.
- nodes:
  - spec: kind anchor, instruction, needs [], inputs [], output? anchor nodes — do they need output schema? Probably not required. verify: ["test -f GUIDE.md"], tools maybe [].
  - build: kind execution, needs ["spec"], inputs [{name: "spec", from: "spec", field: ...}]. Hmm, inputs require {name, from, field, fallback?}. The spec anchor needs an output schema to have a field... Anchors run shell commands; do they produce output? The audit checks "every node output consumed" and "one declared edge and artifact per dependency". For build's input from spec, I need a field. Let me give spec an output schema, e.g. {"type":"object","properties":{"ok":{"type":"boolean"}},"required":["ok"],"additionalProperties":false}. Anchors may not return output though. Hmm.

The audit rules: "acyclic needs with one declared edge and artifact per dependency; every node output consumed". So each needs dependency needs an edge with artifact, and each node's output must be consumed by some edge. If spec has no output, there's nothing to consume — maybe fine. But if build declares input from spec, does the anchor output exist? Risky. I could give build no inputs at all, just needs: ["spec"] with an edges anchors from spec→build with artifact "GUIDE.md exists". That satisfies "one declared edge and artifact per dependency". Then build has inputs: [] maybe. For L2, "an anchor with verify commands and a fresh verification node" — satisfied.

But wait, is an anchor's output required to be consumed? If anchor has no output declared, no issue.

- check: kind verification, needs ["build"], contextScope "fresh-independent", tools ["read"], inputs [{name:"draft", from:"build", field:"heading"}], output {"type":"object","properties":{"verdict":{"type":"string","enum":["pass","fail"]}},"required":["verdict"],"additionalProperties":false}.
- report: kind synthesis, needs ["check"], tools [], inputs [{name:"verdict", from:"check", field:"verdict"}], output {"type":"object","properties":{"summary":{"type":"string"}},"required":["summary"],"additionalProperties":false}.

Edges:
- {from:"spec", to:"build", relation:"anchors", artifact:"GUIDE.md exists on disk"}
- {from:"build", to:"check", relation:"verifies", artifact:"heading value and path used"}
- {from:"check", to:"report", relation:"feeds", artifact:"review verdict", allowedFields:["verdict"]}
- loop edge: {from:"check", to:"build", relation:"feeds", artifact:"review verdict", allowedFields:["verdict"], cycleGuard:{maxIterations:2, until:"test -f loop.marker || { touch loop.marker; exit 1; }"}}

Wait — the until command: `test -f loop.marker || { touch loop.marker; exit 1; }` — first time: file doesn't exist → touch it and exit 1 → until fails → loop runs again (fired once). Second time: file exists → exit 0 → until satisfied → loop stops. So loop fires once. Unless... the loop fires and build+check re-run, then until checked again. So fire count 1.

But careful: does the shell working directory persist? Probably in workspace. Fine.

Also: "Only the from node of a loop may feed nodes outside it." The from node is "check", which feeds "report" — is report inside the loop? The loop is check→build; build needs spec, check needs build. report needs check, so report is downstream of check, not part of the loop (loop = build → check → build). Hmm, "Only the from node of a loop may feed nodes outside it" — report is fed by check, which is the from node of the loop. So that's fine.

Also, budget per attempt maybe optional. Let me add budgets modestly: nodes budget {steps: 3, wallMs: 60000}. Actually budget is per attempt with steps/tokens/wallMs. Keep it simple, maybe omit budgets. Audit checks "the run budget" — maybe requires budget somewhere? Let me include budget on each node to be safe: {steps: 4, wallMs: 120000}.

retryBudget maybe 0 or 1.

Anchor node output schema: do anchors require output? Let's try with no output for spec, and build's inputs empty.

Also the edges: "every node output consumed" — build's output consumed by check (field heading). check's output consumed by report (field verdict). report's output consumed by... nothing. Synthesis output is the deliverable presumably; audit may require output consumed only for non-terminal? Hmm, "every node output consumed" — if taken literally, report's output must be consumed by an edge. But there is no consumer. Maybe the deliverable covers it. Let's try and see what audit says; I can add output to edges as consumed. Actually maybe declare an edge from report to... nothing. Let's just try.

Also need to tell every node that reads to pass exactly relative path GUIDE.md. So build instruction: "Use the read tool with path exactly 'GUIDE.md' (relative, never absolute)." check instruction similarly.

runInputs: [] — I think fine.

Also "at L2, an anchor with verify commands and a fresh verification node" — check has contextScope fresh-independent. Good.

Let me write the plan JSON. No bash calls by me — the instructions say only call graph_capabilities, graph_audit, graph_run, graph_query. Done.

Let me construct.

Node spec: kind "anchor", instruction "Confirm GUIDE.md exists in the workspace root at the relative path GUIDE.md. Do not read or modify anything else.", needs [], inputs [], verify ["test -f GUIDE.md"], tools [], writes [], budget {steps: 1, wallMs: 30000}, retryBudget 0.

Hmm, anchor node's output → maybe not needed.

Node build: kind execution, instruction: "Read the first heading of GUIDE.md. Call the read tool exactly once with file_path set to the relative path GUIDE.md (never an absolute path). Return the first markdown heading line (e.g. '# Title') as the string value of heading.", needs ["spec"], inputs [], output schema with heading string, tools ["read"], contextScope "fresh-independent"? Not required. writes [] (read-only task).

Node check: kind verification, instruction: "Independently verify the first heading of GUIDE.md. Call the read tool exactly once with file_path set to the relative path GUIDE.md (never an absolute path). Compare the first heading in the file with the received heading; return verdict pass if they match, fail otherwise.", needs ["build"], inputs [{name:"claimed", from:"build", field:"heading"}], output verdict enum, tools ["read"], contextScope "fresh-independent", budget.

Node report: kind synthesis, needs ["check"], inputs [{name:"verdict", from:"check", field:"verdict"}], tools [], output summary.

Edges as above. Note: edges must include allowedFields optional.

Loop edge: from check to build, relation feeds, artifact "review verdict", allowedFields ["verdict"], cycleGuard {maxIterations: 2, until: "test -f loop.marker || { touch loop.marker; exit 1; }"}.

Note: build is fed by the anchor edge and the loop edge. "one declared edge and artifact per dependency" — build depends on spec (edge spec→build) plus loop edge from check. Two incoming edges... the loop edge isn't in needs, so fine? The rule "acyclic needs with one declared edge and artifact per dependency" — dependency = needs. Build's needs = ["spec"], edge exists. OK.

The deliverable: "The first heading of GUIDE.md." acceptance: list, e.g. ["graph_run completes with stop reason COMPLETE", "report.summary states the first heading of GUIDE.md"] } — hmm, better acceptance: ["The first heading of GUIDE.md is reported"] . Acceptance non-empty list. Frozen after first version, so I should get it right first time.
